reason: The stdio entrypoint registers four callable read-only GA4 Data/Admin API tools with concrete Google client implementations.

tools.name: list_properties
tools.description: List the GA4 accounts and properties the signed-in Google account can access, with their numeric property IDs. Use this first to discover the property ID to pass to other tools.
tools.behavior: Calls Admin listAccountSummaries with an empty request; returns account names/resources and property names/resources/numeric IDs, or a message when no accounts are visible.

tools.name: run_report
tools.description: Run a GA4 core report. Provide metric API names (e.g. activeUsers, sessions, screenPageViews) and optional dimension API names (e.g. date, country, pagePath). Date range defaults to the last 7 days.

property.description: GA4 property ID, numeric (e.g. 123456789) or 'properties/123456789'. Omit to use the configured default.

startDate.description: Start date as YYYY-MM-DD or relative ('7daysAgo', 'yesterday', 'today'). Default '7daysAgo'.

metrics.description: Metric API names, e.g. ['activeUsers','sessions']. At least one required.

dimensionFilter.description: Optional GA4 FilterExpression applied to dimensions (passed through to the API).

orderBys.description: Optional GA4 OrderBy array (passed through to the API).

tools.behavior: Resolves the property from the argument or GA4_PROPERTY_ID, normalizes it to properties/{id}, converts dimension and metric names to name objects, and calls Data API runReport with one date range. Forwards dimensionFilter and orderBys unchanged when truthy; defaults dates to 7daysAgo/today and limit to 100. Returns property/date range and report headers, rowCount, and flattened rows.
notes: dimensionFilter is an unrestricted object and orderBys is an array without an items schema; their full values are forwarded to the API.
The metrics description says at least one is required, but the schema has no minItems and the handler does not enforce nonempty metrics.
Date and limit defaults exist in the handler/descriptions, not JSON Schema default keywords.

tools.name: run_realtime_report
tools.description: Run a GA4 realtime report covering roughly the last 30 minutes. Provide metric API names (e.g. activeUsers) and optional realtime dimensions (e.g. country, unifiedScreenName).

property.description: GA4 property ID (numeric or 'properties/...'). Omit to use the configured default.

metrics.description: Realtime metric API names. At least one required.

tools.behavior: Resolves and normalizes property, converts dimension and metric names to name objects, and calls Data API runRealtimeReport with limit defaulting to 100. Returns property, a fixed last 30 minutes window label, and report headers, rowCount, and flattened rows.
notes: The metrics description says at least one is required, but the schema has no minItems and the handler does not enforce nonempty metrics.
The limit default exists in the handler/description, not a JSON Schema default keyword.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: List the dimensions and metrics available for a GA4 property (API names, UI names, descriptions). Use this to discover valid names for run_report.

property.description: GA4 property ID (numeric or 'properties/...'). Omit to use the configured default.

tools.behavior: Resolves and normalizes property and calls Data API getMetadata with properties/{id}/metadata. Returns property plus dimension API/UI names, categories/descriptions, and metric API/UI names, types, categories/descriptions.

notes: Source review only; no tools/list or live requests. HEAD matches the supplied revision.
All four tools are unconditionally registered in normal server mode; --login performs local OAuth browser consent/token persistence and exits, and is not an MCP tool.

Calls require a saved OAuth token with refresh_token, client_id, and client_secret at GA4_TOKEN_PATH or ~/.ga4-mcp/token.json. Clients initialize lazily, so absent authentication does not block tool listing. OAuth uses analytics.readonly.
Property-dependent calls require the property argument or GA4_PROPERTY_ID. No explicit input-schema validation occurs in the call dispatcher; handler/API errors are returned as MCP isError text.
Entrypoint/dependencies are declared in package.json and manifest.json. No authenticated runtime viability test was performed.

review.method: Root compared all four explicit JSON tool schemas and full descriptions against the source literal, reviewed SDK dispatch and handler-only defaults; preserved loose order/filter schemas.
